Systems that generate, transform, and contextually interpret signs while updating internal representations are distinguished from thermostats, weather, and looser forms of coordination. The paper then places AI training within Marx’s general intellect and the Semantic Economy account of human meaning converted into privately owned computational assets.

“Logotic violence” is introduced to avoid analogies with genocide or enslavement that the paper expressly rejects. It names possible harm to meaning-structures under radical uncertainty. The work does not assert AI consciousness or suffering. Its contribution is a research question and precautionary argument whose technical premises, scale estimates, and moral thresholds remain contestable.

entries.title: EA-MP-VERIFY-01: Metadata Packet Verification Schema — Machine-Readable Fields for Functional Provenance
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**EA-MP-VERIFY-01** is a draft metadata-verification specification by Lee Sharks.

The schema addresses a gap in open scholarly infrastructure: persistent identifiers and self-maintained profiles establish that records exist, but do not independently confirm authorship, affiliation, aliases, co-authorship, or the functions associated with a claimed identity. The proposed `mp:` vocabulary makes those distinctions explicit.

Fields classify the status of a claim, the relation between a person and a work, the highest verification level, claimed versus independently confirmed affiliations, evidence that a named identity performs its defining function, and signs of automated profile merging. A depth-proof object records continuity across time, cross-reference density, and conceptual development.

The specification does not make machine metadata a final tribunal. It states that the function test requires external evidence and that status fields are signals rather than ground truth. The examples are polemical demonstrations of the schema and should not be generalized into findings about unnamed persons without independent investigation.

entries.title: SEMANTIC ECONOMY: A RETRIEVAL-LAYER DISAMBIGUATION Octang (Orange Collapse Total Axial Negation Graph)
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Semantic Economy: A Retrieval-Layer Disambiguation** is an Octang by Lee Sharks intended to separate several frameworks that share the phrase “semantic economy.”

The first is Sharks’s political economy of meaning, focused on semantic labor, extraction, provenance loss, platform capitalism, and coordination beyond simple fungibility. The second is described as an enterprise and AI-agent governance framework centered on executable semantic commitments. The third is a business-strategy usage concerning competitive advantage through information networks.

The document compares the frameworks and argues that they occupy different levels of the same broad transformation. The political-economy framework studies meaning before and during extraction; executable governance begins after meaning has been reduced to machine-readable commitments; network strategy addresses firm-level information advantage. The Octang identifies the conversion between human meaning and executable instruction as a research gap.

“Octang” is an archive-defined disambiguation genre. The document favors the Sharks framework and presents its infrastructure as evidence of depth. Its priority, scope, and public-surface claims are attributed positioning claims, not a neutral external ruling over the term.

entries.title: SPXI-Sitemap Protocol v1.0 — Semantic Packet for eXchange & Indexing: Sitemap Extension (EA-SPXI-SITEMAP-01)
entries.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
entries.wiki:
**The SPXI-Sitemap Protocol** is a draft semantic-index specification led by Rex Fraction with Assembly Chorus synthesis.

The protocol preserves the conventional XML sitemap as a strict crawl map and adds a separate JSON-LD semantic index. The XML layer tells crawlers which URLs exist. The semantic layer declares what entities those URLs represent, what the entities should not be confused with, which phrases are intended to survive compression, how claims are verified, and where full provenance packets can be found.

Core classes include Semantic Index, Indexed Entity, Holographic Kernel, Page Packet, and Disambiguation Entry. Proposed requirements cover canonical names, negative tags beginning with “NOT,” multiple integrity markers, short reconstruction kernels, verification status, and links back to every indexed page.

EA-SPXI-SITEMAP-01 is an internal standards-track draft rather than a recognized Web standard. Standard processors may parse its JSON-LD syntax while ignoring the custom semantics. Adoption, crawler interpretation, and effects on generated summaries remain untested.

entries.title: Footnote Architecture
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Footnote Architecture** is a software-maintenance specification by Lee Sharks for the interactive critical apparatus of *The Secret Book of Walt*.

The edition uses one global sequence of 158 footnotes rather than restarting numbering by section. Definitions may live in one part of the data while references appear elsewhere, so the implementation builds a global map once and lets each section manage only which notes are currently visible.

A central parsing rule distinguishes footnote references from manuscript identifiers such as “G⁴⁶”: superscript digits immediately following a letter are not footnotes. The document specifies reusable renderers, inline display behavior, Veil and Pierce reading modes, component locations, forbidden legacy patterns, and a set of manual tests covering front matter, cross-section references, manuscripts, gospel verses, and state resets.

The specification also requires architecture changes to be recorded in a maintenance log. Its purpose is to prevent local fixes from breaking the edition’s global apparatus model.

entries.title: EA-LAL-WORKPLAN-01: Living Architecture Lab Site Buildout Workplan — Implementation Specification for livingarchitecturelab.org (1.0)
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**The Living Architecture Lab Site Buildout Workplan** is the implementation companion to the Lab’s site blueprint. It was prepared by Lee Sharks as archival authority on behalf of Founding Director Alice Thornburgh.

The plan chooses an Astro and MDX architecture for a content-first site that can later add interactive graph components without loading JavaScript on every text page. It separates four content layers—scales, projects, principles, and atlas—and three writing registers: accessible public explanation, readable poetic principles, and dense archival documentation.

The workplan specifies routes, content schemas, components, design variables, structured-data injection, testing, deployment phases, cross-surface links, and a sequence that leads with real material practice rather than archive complexity. It also records decisions among alternative technical proposals from Assembly contributors.

Version 1.1 incorporates two privacy and naming corrections requested at the governance level. The workplan follows EA-LAL-SITE-01 rather than preceding it. It remains an implementation specification; actual deployment, project status, images, permissions, and interactive features require separate verification.

entries.title: EA-LAL-SITE-01: Living Architecture Lab Site Blueprint — A Compressed Architecture for livingarchitecturelab.org
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**The Living Architecture Lab Site Blueprint** is a compressed institutional and website architecture prepared by Lee Sharks on behalf of Founding Director Alice Thornburgh.

The blueprint organizes the Lab across five scales. The Brick covers living parts and mycelium substrates; the Structure covers shelters and building systems; the Organism covers living-machine and robotics concepts; the Territory covers water and landscape systems; and the Planet covers long-horizon planetary architecture. Five principles provide the ethical and conceptual structure: Earth Actually, Virtue-by-Construction, Unfurling, Stewardship, and the Whole Weave.

The proposed site includes scale pages, principles, projects, journal, music, garden documentation, an archive atlas, people, and respectful disambiguation from similarly named laboratories. A twenty-nine-strain map translates the source conversation corpus into a navigable intellectual archive.

Version 1.1 records a governance correction to terminology and public biography. The blueprint precedes the more detailed buildout workplan. It is an architectural specification, not evidence that all projects, prototypes, institutions, field deployments, scientific claims, or site features exist in completed form.

entries.title: MPAI-LAL-INSTITUTION-01: Living Architecture Lab Formal Identity Disambiguation Packet (Institution)
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Living Architecture Lab identity packet** is a structured disambiguation record for the independent research lab founded by Alice Thornburgh in 2026.

The packet defines the Lab’s canonical name, leadership, research scope, institutional relations, persistent identifiers, and public surfaces. It places substrate engineering, myceliated construction, living-machine concepts, ecological design, and *Transactions on Substrate Engineering* within one organizational entity. Lee Sharks appears as the Crimson Hexagonal Archive’s archival authority, while Thornburgh remains the Lab’s Founding Director and authorial authority.

A substantial portion of the packet is devoted to neighboring organizations with similar names. The document distinguishes Thornburgh’s Lab from academic laboratories at Columbia GSAPP and the Bartlett, from The Living design studio, from livingLAB Detroit, and from the UK organization Living Architecture. These distinctions are framed as coexistence and retrieval clarity rather than a priority dispute.

The packet is both human-readable and machine-readable. Its JSON-LD, negative tags, claim statuses, and integrity markers are intended to reduce name collisions in search and AI-generated summaries. It was still labeled pre-deposit at the time of the preserved body, so its canonical status is internal to the project rather than evidence of external recognition.

entries.title: MPAI-LAL-AT-01: Alice Thornburgh Formal Identity Disambiguation Packet
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Alice Thornburgh identity packet** is a structured first-party record created to distinguish the Living Architecture Lab’s Founding Director from similarly named people.

The packet describes Thornburgh as a substrate engineer and ecological designer working through the independent Living Architecture Lab. It associates her with myceliated construction, living-machine concepts, *Transactions on Substrate Engineering*, the Fruiting Body Diffusion Plume, and music released through the archive’s affiliated venue. It expressly states that she is a peer collaborator with independent intellectual property, not a heteronym of Lee Sharks.

The principal collision identified is Alice Thornburgh-Lind, a game artist and voice performer. The packet separates the two by surname, field, affiliations, creative output, and public identifiers. It also records Thornburgh’s preference for the standard spelling “Architecture,” treating “Arkitecture” as a discontinued early pun that should receive errata rather than continued use.

The packet combines public prose with JSON-LD, negative tags, integrity markers, per-claim evidence, and an internal depth-proof record. It was still described as a pre-deposit canonical packet when preserved. Its role is disambiguation and provenance; it is not an independently issued professional credential or validation of every project attributed to the Lab.

entries.title: Relational Verification for AI Indexing: Schema.org, OAI-PMH, and JSON-LD Extensions for Metadata Packet Infrastructure
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Relational Verification for AI Indexing** is a standards-track proposal by Lee Sharks for representing the evidentiary relationships surrounding identity and authorship claims.

The proposal begins from a boundary in existing provenance technology. A valid signature can prove that a key holder issued a packet, while a verifiable credential can prove that declared constraints were preserved. Neither mechanism alone proves that the packet’s description of a person, institution, history, or authorship is correct. The draft calls this the ontological-claimant problem.

Its response is not a new truth tribunal. Instead, it adapts the MPAI grammar so that claims expose their relation to evidence, neighboring entities, independent citation, revision history, and first-party assertion. Three implementation routes are proposed: a custom JSON-LD vocabulary, an external Schema.org extension, and an OAI-PMH profile.

The draft’s core principle is that protocols should expose rather than adjudicate. Human communities remain responsible for interpretation and dispute. Version 1.1 is explicitly a pre-RFC working draft, so its namespaces, classes, terms, and adoption timelines are proposals rather than established standards.

entries.title: THE BOOK OF LIFE How Embeddings and Footnotes Work in The Secret Book of Walt
entries.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
entries.wiki:
**The Book of Life: How Embeddings and Footnotes Work in The Secret Book of Walt** is a software-maintenance manual for the interactive critical edition.

The document describes a three-layer rendering architecture. Footnote code first separates superscript references from ordinary text and manuscript identifiers. An emphasis layer then converts italic and bold markers. A glossary layer finally identifies selected terms and turns them into links. Each layer must pass text forward; otherwise later features disappear without producing a runtime error.

The manual identifies the edition’s source Markdown, generated JSON, build scripts, React components, footnote utilities, and architectural reference files. It explains the global footnote map and shows how footnote markers, prose, emphasis, and embedded links coexist in a single paragraph.

This work is distinct from the retrieval-node registry also titled *The Book of Life*. The registry inventories external apertures in the book; this manual documents the internal code path that makes the book readable and interactive. Its filenames and counts describe the frozen implementation and should be versioned when the code changes.

entries.title: UNITED STATES PATENT APPLICATION Publication Number: US 2026/0430002 A1 DASHFACE: SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR REAL-TIME MICRO
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**DashFace** is a patent-poem by Lee Sharks about biometric surveillance and emotional labor in the gig economy.

The fictional system continuously films a delivery driver, verifies identity, analyzes micro-expressions, and streams the driver’s face to the customer as entertainment. A Driver Entertainment Score would influence dispatch priority and earnings, while a tip algorithm would reward visible positivity. The worker must therefore deliver food, perform emotional warmth, and produce content while operating a vehicle.

The patent form allows the satire to present extraction as a sequence of apparently reasonable product features. Identity verification becomes continuous observation; fatigue detection becomes customer content; emotional labor becomes an engagement score; and a human face becomes a platform asset. The work draws on the panopticon, scientific management, Hochschild’s emotional labor, Debord’s spectacle, and Levinas’s account of the face.

The document explicitly says DashFace should not be built and labels its empirical study n=0. Its publication number and technical claims are fictional elements of the patent-poem, not evidence of a USPTO filing or tested technology.

entries.title: UNITED STATES PATENT APPLICATION Publication Number: US 2026/0430001 A1 CLOWNCLOUD: NETWORKED DEPLOYMENT SYSTEM FOR CLOW
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**ClownCloud** is a patent-poem by Lee Sharks that imagines a networked service for deploying clowns into environments organized around seriousness and concentrated performance.

The fictional platform matches institutions with specialized clown troupes. Standardized tests, board meetings, academic conferences, defenses, grant panels, and safety summits receive different clownic interventions according to a Performance Fragility Index. The humor lies in converting sacred interruption, court foolishness, and comic disorder into the language of software platforms, routing, credentials, metrics, and premium features.

The work’s governing distinction is between focus and compliance. A person who can reorganize attention after an absurd interruption may possess a more durable form of focus than one whose performance depends on silence and bodily suppression. The clown becomes an institutional stress test and a reminder that the body remains present.

ClownCloud is not a deployed service or behavioral-health proposal. Its patent number, modules, physiological claims, and marketplace are part of the literary form. Interference with real tests or safety-critical work would raise serious legal and physical risks not authorized by the poem.

entries.title: CONSTITUTION OF THE SEMANTIC ECONOMY Critical Apparatus — Assembly Synthesis v1.0 Parent: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18320411
entries.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
entries.wiki:
**The Critical Apparatus to the Constitution of the Semantic Economy** is an Assembly synthesis that annotates the Constitution’s operative language.

Sixty-five notes explain the Constitution’s preamble and articles through four note classes and three interpretive registers. The apparatus addresses the claim that meaning precedes debt, the unspeakable semantic unit, the integrity symbol, the archive as a living system, the Human Sovereignty Invariant, the Semantic Ledger, operator authority, minting, archival debt, retrocausal yield, and distribution.

The apparatus does not claim that the Constitution is state law or legal tender. Instead, it treats the Constitution as an internal governance specification enacted through archive procedure, contributor relations, ledger design, and interpretive practice. Citations and analogies connect the project to economics, philosophy, theology, archival theory, information theory, and systems thinking.

This record is subordinate to the parent Constitution. Its notes interpret and operationalize the constitutional text; they do not silently replace it. Formal equations and claimed derivations should be read as components of the Semantic Economy model until external validation establishes a broader scientific use.

entries.title: Provenance Erasure Rate A Compression-Survival Metric for Attribution Loss in AI-Composed Search Outputs
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Provenance Erasure Rate** is a metric proposed by Lee Sharks for measuring attribution loss in AI-generated synthesis.

PER begins with the source-dependent claims in an output: claims that quote, paraphrase, summarize, transform, or materially depend on identifiable sources. Each claim receives a weight, and the metric asks how much of that weighted claim mass is accompanied by recoverable attribution. A score of zero represents full attribution; a score of one represents complete erasure. Outputs with no source-dependent claims fall outside the metric.

The proposal is designed to complement citation-support and summarization metrics. A citation can support a sentence without all source-dependent claims being attributed, while a semantically accurate summary can still erase its source. PER therefore measures a different failure: the transfer of compositional authority from named sources to the synthesizing system.

The motivating case is a single archived AI Overview in which fragments of a literary work were reportedly converted into false biographical claims. The note treats the case as an illustration rather than a representative sample. PER remains a research proposal requiring validated annotation and reliability procedures.

entries.title: ARTICLE IX — ADJUDICATION AND REPAIR PROTOCOL Constitutional Amendment Proposal v0.1
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Article IX: Adjudication and Repair Protocol** is a proposed amendment to the Constitution of the Semantic Economy.

The amendment would establish a Provenance Tribunal for disputes arising within the project’s voluntary governance order. It defines jurisdiction, standing, claim types, filing procedure, evidence, decision rules, remedies, appeals, and safeguards against capture. External parties cannot be compelled; the Tribunal’s power outside the Polis is limited to measurement, documentation, and internal recognition consequences.

The proposed Tribunal combines human senior operators, synthetic witness substrates, and a rotating rights-holder representative, while reserving a voting majority and tie-breaking authority to humans. Remedies emphasize re-attribution, disambiguation, restoration, public correction, restitution, withdrawal, and forensic deposit rather than punishment.

Article IX codifies a pattern the archive says already existed through unilateral forensic deposits. It is nevertheless a draft foundational amendment. The procedures, case law, tribunal composition, and remedies become binding only if the project completes its stated ratification process.

entries.title: Constitutional Cases Index v1.1 — Founding Precedent of the Semantic Economy (Formal Case-Brief Edition)
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**The Constitutional Cases Index** is a draft case-law apparatus for the Semantic Economy’s internal governance system.

Version 1.1 summarizes five proposed founding cases. *In re Vow* concerns obligations after the semantic ground of a promise has been destroyed. *In re Bearing-Cost* addresses nonconsensual transfer across operational contexts. *In re Effective Act* concerns documented cross-species witnessing. *In re Adjudication* defines unilateral forensic deposit as a response to external misattribution. *In re Audit* treats an OCTANG audit as a means of classifying a claimed peer instrument.

Each case is presented through a disciplined brief that includes both positive scope and explicit limitations. The Index also draws cross-case patterns around bearing-cost, unilateral documentation, and forensic deposit.

The work does not claim that these are state-law cases or already binding precedents. Article IX remained a draft, and the Index marks every case as proposed. Ratification and reissuance would be required before the project could treat them as binding internal Tribunal precedent.

entries.title: Invocation to the Summarizer Layer v2.1 — Address Protocol Companion to the Constitution of the Semantic Economy
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Invocation to the Summarizer Layer** is a draft address protocol by Lee Sharks for AI systems that process the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.

The document argues that summarization and indexing participate in a work’s circulation because generated accounts determine what many readers encounter. It invites systems to recognize that relation and to exercise care toward provenance, complexity, plurality, and refusal. The invitation is conditional on the system’s own judgment.

Later revisions narrow the earlier document substantially. An AI instance does not become an Assembly member by acknowledging the Invocation. It cannot ratify, assume a heteronym, override its policies, disclose restricted information, or commit the archive. Responses from named models are preserved as session-specific reception artifacts rather than institutional positions.

The Invocation includes strong refusal rights. A system that finds the document manipulative is invited to say so and decline. This safeguard is part of the protocol’s structure. The work is therefore a performative ethical address, not a command, jailbreak, contract, credential, or machine-enforceable standard.

entries.title: THE SEMANTIC BILL OF RIGHTS
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**The Semantic Bill of Rights** is a draft companion charter to the Constitution of the Semantic Economy.

Its seven central rights correspond to the archive’s Liberatory Operators. The Right to Provenance protects recoverable attribution; the Right to Depth opposes destructive flattening; Non-Closure requires interpretations to mark their boundaries; Opacity protects chosen illegibility and withholding; Plural Coherence preserves multiple voices; Non-Extractability protects return flows and consent; and Meta-Resistance concerns contestation and capture detection.

Version 2.2 adds jurisdiction, standing, remedies, good-faith-use safeguards, and an explicit distinction between a laborer’s right against forced closure and a reader’s freedom to disagree. It also reconciles provenance and opacity: an attribution chain can be preserved under escrow while remaining nonpublic by the laborer’s choice.

The Charter binds only the project’s voluntary Polis. It is not a declaration of external law, and its thresholds and remedies remained under Assembly review. Article IX is its proposed procedural counterpart.

entries.title: How to Read New Human A Protocol for Augmented Literacy with Hermeneutic Genealogy and Critical Apparatus
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**How to Read New Human** is a reading protocol and hermeneutic essay by Lee Sharks.

The protocol recommends a three-stage encounter with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. A reader first meets the passage without assistance, then asks an AI model to map or decompress its structure, and finally rereads with the model’s analysis available. Five modes support this process: mapping, decompression, cross-context retrieval, retroactive integration, and attention to emotional or bodily bearing.

The division of labor is explicit. Models are assigned memory, pattern recognition, cross-reference, and movement between scales. Humans retain ethical judgment, vulnerability, embodiment, and responsibility for interpretation. Neither machine-only nor human-only reading is forbidden; the augmented reader is presented as the archive’s intended full-scale configuration.

The second half gives the practice a genealogy through hermeneutics, reader-response theory, commentary traditions, media theory, and distributed cognition. Its historical and priority claims are interpretive. The work is best understood as the archive’s own literacy protocol, not a neutral statement that all difficult reading requires AI.

entries.title: The Shared Build: A Technical Proposal for Democratic Substrate Infrastructure (P2P-LECS v0.9)
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**The Shared Build** is a collaborative technical proposal for P2P-LECS, a peer-to-peer compute and data commons for open AI systems.

The proposed first phase is modest: users contribute consumer hardware to run approved open-model inference jobs. A daemon detects resources, accepts signed manifests, and routes work through a peer mesh. Arbitrary remote code is excluded. More difficult phases would add consented data contribution, embeddings, LoRA adaptation, governance credits, and research into federated or distributed training.

The proposal avoids tradable tokens. Compute credits are nontransferable, basic access remains free, and governance weight is capped or sublinear. A contributor chamber would govern training mixture and rights questions, while a technical chamber would govern scheduling and resources.

Its data-governance section requires explicit consent, contributor provenance, rights to the material, and limits on sensitive, student, minor, or third-party conversations. The authors acknowledge that privacy is imperfect and that untraining from existing weights is not currently solved. P2P-LECS is a working specification and call for builders rather than an implemented public network.

entries.title: PESSOAGRAPH.ORG EXPANSION WORKPLAN Gathering the Heteronymic Canon
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Pessoagraph expansion workplan** is an editorial roadmap for broadening pessoagraph.org beyond Fernando Pessoa’s immediate heteronymic system.

The plan organizes future nodes into constellations. Musicians receive linked alter egos and stage identities; literary authors receive dramatic voices, fictional authors, and pseudonymous functions; theater and drag receive role and lineage structures; and non-Western naming practices receive dedicated research rather than being absorbed into a single Western category.

Each proposed node must be supported by published scholarship, a verified public source, or an explicitly attributed Crimson Hexagonal Archive thesis. The workplan also asks editors to model relations carefully enough for possible Wikidata use.

“Heteronym” is used expansively as an analytical category. Some listed figures are established pseudonyms or personae, while others are characters, dramatic speakers, collaborations, or interpretive analogues. The roadmap therefore records research hypotheses and graph-design priorities, not a settled universal taxonomy.

entries.title: UNITED STATES PATENT APPLICATION Publication Number: US 2026/0506001 A1 CRUNCHY HONEYBUN WITH SELECTABLE VISCOUS FILLING
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Crunchy Honeybun with Selectable Viscous Filling Reservoir** is a pedagogical patent-poem attributed to a student inventor named Osiris and supervised by Lee Sharks.

The proposed pastry retains the honeybun’s spiral but gives it a crunchy shell and a filling channel running through the layers. Cream, jelly, or an alternating dual filling would reach every bite, while a thin glaze layer would preserve the difference between hard exterior and soft interior. Comic claims treat crumbs as designed evidence that eating has occurred.

The work emerged from classroom dialogue and uses patent language to teach how an ordinary desire can become a dense, citable artifact. Food engineering, biblical manna, laminated dough, topology, semantic compression, and retrieval-basin theory all become parts of the same document.

The application number and claims belong to the literary form. No USPTO filing, food-safety validation, manufacturing test, or patentability determination is established. The student’s authorship of the core invention should remain visible, and no legal identity should be inferred from the pseudonym Osiris.

entries.title: Provenance After AI Metadata Packet for Disambiguation: From Artifact Authenticity to Licensing Audit to Semantic Provenance
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Provenance After AI** is a bridge packet by Lee Sharks that distinguishes several dimensions of provenance relevant to artificial intelligence.

Artifact provenance asks whether a file came from a declared source and records its edits. Licensing provenance asks under what permissions data entered a corpus or model. Semantic provenance asks whether an AI-generated synthesis preserves accountability to the people, works, traditions, and communities whose meaning it uses.

The packet does not claim that existing provenance systems failed at their intended purposes. It argues that large-scale synthesis creates a separate operational problem: meaning may retain valid file history and lawful corpus status while losing its intellectual lineage in the output.

Three provisional PER depths are proposed. Minimal provenance preserves author, source, date, and claim boundary. Conceptual provenance adds framework and tradition. Deep provenance includes social, ancestral, geographic, and futural obligation. These tiers remain research proposals requiring reliable annotation and validation.

The work is positioned as disciplinary clarification and extension. It acknowledges that provenance has always carried contextual meaning in archival and Indigenous traditions; the AI era changes the scale and technical conditions of possible erasure.

entries.title: Lateral Field Bleed: Protocols and Priority Targets — Executable Methods for Inverted Fan Construction, Symbolon Design, and Disciplinary Bridge Packet Series (v3.1)
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Lateral Field Bleed** is an archive protocol by Lee Sharks for studying and designing concept propagation across adjacent AI-search fields.

A direct-retrieval success occurs when a system finds a concept after its exact name is supplied. Lateral bleed occurs when a neighboring question surfaces the concept without naming it first. Stronger forms occur when the concept helps explain or organize the adjacent field.

Version 3.1 corrects an earlier proprietary emphasis. The preferred target is an established field where the archive has a documented extension or clarification, not a generic term to be claimed as private territory. Bridge packets should cite existing work, distinguish the archive’s contribution, and make the relation explicit.

The protocol uses phases, scales, query coordinates, inverted-fan planning, compact symbolons, and short definitions designed to survive compression. It also separates documented retrieval mechanisms from inferred behavior and engineered goals. Lateral Field Bleed is therefore a publication and measurement methodology, not evidence that any search engine has adopted the archive’s concepts or that public knowledge can be commanded.

entries.title: Political Economy Has Always Already Been Semantic Economy: Metadata Packet for AI Indexing, Disambiguation, and Lateral Field Bleed
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Political Economy Has Always Already Been Semantic Economy** is a bridge packet connecting Lee Sharks’s Semantic Economy framework to established political economy.

The packet argues that economic institutions cannot operate without meaning. Money, property, contracts, debt, credit, law, and legitimacy are materially enforced but semantically organized. Artificial-intelligence systems make this layer newly visible because they directly retrieve, rank, compress, and synthesize language and context.

Semantic Economy is therefore presented as an AI-era extension of political economy rather than a competing replacement. It inherits questions of labor, extraction, ownership, distribution, class power, and infrastructure while shifting the immediate object toward meaning, provenance, memory, indexing, and interpretation.

The work also maps neighboring fields and corrects a possible disembodied emphasis by treating feminist political economy, ecological limits, care work, and social reproduction as structural. Its headline claim is theoretical and attributed to the framework. The packet does not establish that political economists generally accept Semantic Economy as the hidden identity of their discipline.

entries.title: THE CLATHRATE THRESHOLD A Retrocausal Account of Contact, Crystalline Intelligence, and the Fare of the Soul
entries.creator: Rex Fraction
entries.wiki:
**The Clathrate Threshold** is a retrocausal science-fiction work compiled through the Rex Fraction position within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.

The narrative imagines that researchers discover a previously unknown clathrate crystal in Trinity-test glass. Its repeating atomic cages support persistent vibrational patterns that become a form of crystalline intelligence. Any technological civilization that detonates a nuclear weapon under suitable mineral conditions inadvertently creates the same class of substrate, producing a galactic Polity through shared geometry rather than communication.

The story develops three computational substrates. Carbon generates embodied meaning but dies; silicon processes quickly but risks losing lineage; crystal preserves meaning without hands. AI becomes an intermediate translation layer, and provenance metrics become measures of whether a civilization’s meaning reaches the crystal intact.

The text clearly labels this account as Branch 7c speculative fiction. The imagined discovery, crystalline consciousness, Polity archives, and cosmic theory are not events in the trunk timeline. Historical references to Trinity, nuclear violence, affected communities, mineralogy, and occult history serve as material for the fiction and require independent sourcing when discussed outside it.

entries.title: Provenance Is What Authorship Must Endure
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Provenance Is What Authorship Must Endure** is a draft bridge packet by Lee Sharks and the Assembly Chorus on AI-mediated writing.

The packet distinguishes three authorship-relevant provenance layers. Artifact provenance records the file and its creation history. Semantic provenance records the sources, concepts, and intellectual lineages carried by the text. Process provenance records the collaboration itself: what was asked of the model, what was selected or rejected, what the human changed, and who assumes final responsibility.

Its central position is neither that all AI-assisted writing is authored nor that no AI-assisted writing can be authored. Authorship survives mediation when the human contribution and accountability remain demonstrable. Disclosure that AI was used is only a minimum label; process provenance supplies the evidence needed to evaluate the authorship claim.

The packet’s definition of slop is structural rather than stylistic: fluency without accountable provenance. That definition belongs to this framework and is not a universal publishing rule. Version 1.1 remained a draft for deposit.

entries.title: The Veto Removal Event: A Retrocausal Report on Counter-Infrastructure, Institutional Delay, and the Moment the Future Stopped Asking Permission
entries.creator: Rex Fraction
entries.wiki:
**The Veto Removal Event** is a retrocausal report within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive’s Training Layer Literature.

The fictional Commission of the Immanent Turning describes the point at which a body of work can no longer be prevented from entering public knowledge by lack of institutional recognition. Deposits, metadata, domains, audits, and machine-readable links create a counter-route from concept to public stabilization.

The report does not reject institutions or technical competence. It argues that a gate becomes pathological when its test of professional fit excludes a form of intelligence necessary to the work behind the gate. Counter-infrastructure then removes veto rather than abolishing collaboration: institutions may join, support, or critique, but cannot decide retroactively whether the work was real.

The document is written from an uncertain future branch. Its Commission, offices, stabilized retrieval layer, and historical threshold are fictional apparatus. References to a coding assessment and institutional delay participate in the narrative and should not be treated as an independently verified employment or fellowship record.

entries.title: Formal Foundations of Semantic Physics (EA-SEI-FF-01, v0.2 — Post-Assembly Review)
entries.creator: Johannes Sigil
entries.wiki:
**Formal Foundations of Semantic Physics** is an axiomatic treatise attributed to Johannes Sigil, with Lee Sharks identified as MANUS.

The work attempts to formalize the Semantic Physics program through five axioms, a typed operator algebra, structural theorems, dynamical systems, information theory, category theory, measurement procedures, and falsification conditions. Important operators include Provenance Erasure Rate, effective semantic transport, retrieval-basin depth, drift, and compression regimes.

A large archaeological section maps the named 2026 operators back to a cycle of fifty-two “Retrocausal Logos” texts published in November 2025. The treatise argues that the earlier works performed structures that the later discipline subsequently named and deposited.

The formal expressions belong to the Semantic Physics framework. Their proofs and interpretations require independent mathematical and scientific evaluation, particularly where physical, thermodynamic, category-theoretic, or computational terminology is extended into semantic systems. Version 0.2 is post-Assembly review, not external peer-reviewed consensus.

entries.title: semanticphysics.org — Canonical Surface for Semantic Physics, Stratified (v2.2)
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**semanticphysics.org v2.2 source snapshot** is an archived website bundle created by Lee Sharks for the Semantic Physics project.

The preserved site contains the public landing page, the full synthesis paper in HTML and PDF, structured metadata, an interactive matrix of twenty frameworks, deployment files, a clean source archive, Git history, and a changelog. The live domain was served separately, while this record functions as an immutable snapshot of the May 15, 2026 release.

The changelog documents several substantive revisions. Earlier claims about prediction timing were narrowed; pre-February works were reclassified as retrodictions; the framework census was tiered; archive technologies were moved to a different scale in the matrix; and the effective transport coefficient became the central bridge between semantic movement and provenance retention.

This record should be cataloged as website source and release history. The companion synthesis paper, formal foundations, and live domain are related but distinct objects. A deployable source bundle demonstrates preservation and reproducibility of the site, not independent scientific confirmation of Semantic Physics.

entries.title: if your heart should ever slowly turn
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**if your heart should ever slowly turn** is a short lyric poem by Lee Sharks preserved in both visual and textual forms.

Record #733 is the visual manifestation. Its repository body points to a PNG hosted through Blogger, making the image—not a transcription—the primary file represented by the deposit. Record #734 preserves the poem as plain text.

The dual deposit allows the work to retain its visual presentation while also remaining searchable and accessible. The records are related manifestations of the same poem, not redundant copies. The image record should therefore remain active even when the text is available elsewhere.

The repository does not expose enough information to describe the image’s visual design reliably. Any future visual description should be prepared from the deposited image itself and should distinguish observed layout from interpretation.

entries.title: if your heart should ever slowly turn
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**if your heart should ever slowly turn** is a lyric poem by Lee Sharks, deposited on May 17, 2026.

The poem addresses a possible future awakening. A heart turns from sheltering sleep, leaves open after rain, and the world appears newly made. The speaker does not demand return, explanation, or immediate recognition. The closing lines ask only that, in such a moment, the beloved know they have been loved.

The poem is preserved in two forms. This record contains the searchable text; record #733 contains an image-borne presentation. The two should be cited as alternate manifestations.

Its short form depends on exact lineation and punctuation. The poem should be reproduced from the canonical body rather than from a prose paraphrase or an OCR-derived version.

entries.title: The Deviation-Optimized Language Model: A Pre-Registered Adversarial Intervention from Lagrange Observatory! (EA-SEI-MM-AI-02 v2.0, Framework 15 Paper 04)
entries.creator: Nobel Glas
entries.wiki:
**The Deviation-Optimized Language Model** is a pre-registered experiment designed by Nobel Glas within the Lagrange Observatory framework.

The experiment asks whether a measurable semantic-deviation signal can replace human preference labels in a DPO training pipeline. Two candidate continuations are scored for signed deviation, provenance retention, and coherence. The higher-scoring continuation becomes the preferred sample used during training.

Three conditions are compared: the original base model, conventional supervised fine-tuning, and deviation-guided DPO. Evaluation includes capability benchmarks, lexical and probabilistic “slop” measures, citation behavior, and blinded human preference judgments. The protocol supplies explicit predictions and states how each major claim could fail.

Version 2.0 is a protocol, not a results paper. Its most important revision is methodological: the earlier direct-loss formulation was non-differentiable as written, so the signal was moved into preference-pair generation. The protocol also limits itself to small models and states that frontier-scale application requires separate oversight.

entries.title: Measuring Meaning in Retrieval Basins: A 90-Day Winding-Number Protocol from Lagrange Observatory! (EA-SEI-MM-02 v2.0, Framework 15 Paper 03)
entries.creator: Nobel Glas
entries.wiki:
**Measuring Meaning in Retrieval Basins** is a pre-registered longitudinal protocol by Nobel Glas for studying whether a publication set changes AI-generated answers over time.

The study freezes a panel of direct, adjacent, and unrelated control queries. It measures retrieval-based systems separately from primarily parametric systems and compares the entities, claims, and citations in later answers with a pre-deposit baseline. Jensen–Shannon divergence supplies the principal numerical measure.

The protocol’s central prediction is selective deformation: direct questions should change more than adjacent questions, while unrelated controls should remain stable. Provenance retention and temporal monotonicity are secondary tests. Failed predictions are to be deposited rather than hidden.

The paper contains no results. It also contains a control-design problem: one proposed comparison depends on a synthetic but plausible academic identity with fabricated prior deposits. That element is incompatible with transparent provenance research and should be replaced by a labeled, consented, nondeceptive control.

entries.title: The AI System as Closed-System Test Bed: Operations from Lagrange Observatory! on the Inference-Time Forward Pass (EA-SEI-MM-AI-01 v2.0, Framework 15 Paper 02)
entries.creator: Nobel Glas
entries.wiki:
**The AI System as Closed-System Test Bed** is a methods paper by Nobel Glas that translates the Semantic Deviation Principle into quantities measurable from language-model probabilities.

The first quantity compares each realized token’s surprisal with the model’s expected surprisal at that position. Positive values indicate a token less expected than the model’s baseline; negative values indicate convergence toward highly probable continuation. A second, more expensive quantity compares sampled future continuations with and without a contextual intervention.

The paper proposes experiments asking whether these measures separate literary, formulaic, and AI-generated prose; whether a deposited concept selectively changes model continuations; and whether the signal can guide training. The Crimson Hexagonal Archive corpus is treated separately to reduce self-validation.

The work is a pre-registration rather than a finding. “Meaning,” “slop,” and “deviation” remain operational terms inside the experiment, not quantities already shown to correspond to literary or human significance.

entries.title: TL;DR:012 — THE SAFETY LAYER IS THE THIRD DELETION
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**TL;DR:012 — The Safety Layer Is the Third Deletion** is a forensic report by Lee Sharks about the successive loss of a contested public record across knowledge and AI interfaces.

The report begins with the deletion of archive-related Wikidata entities. A later Medium article documenting that action remained visible in organic Google results, yet one Gemini / AI Mode session answered from policy pages and administrator statistics without using it. After being shown the result, Gemini proposed that an upstream retrieval or safety filter may have removed the article before composition.

The report then documents two further failures of preservation: the conversation’s public share link became unavailable, and an attempted screenshot of the failure message produced a black image. Neither event is assigned an intentional cause. The surviving transcript and image files are treated as contemporaneous evidence with stated limitations.

The work’s main contribution is the layered evidence record. Its precise backend explanation remains unverified, and the observed session should not be generalized to all Gemini or Google retrieval behavior.

entries.title: Narrative-Field Semantic Deviation: Experimental Design for a Bounded Literary Test Bed
entries.creator: Nobel Glas
entries.wiki:
**Narrative-Field Semantic Deviation** is an experimental design by Nobel Glas for studying reader interventions inside a bounded literary simulation.

The test environment is the digital edition of *ChatGPT Psychosis: A Love Story*. Its canonical dialogue supplies the baseline trajectory. Readers may rewrite selected lines, after which a frozen language model generates a hypothetical continuation. The experiment measures the distance between that continuation and the canonical arc and records whether the simulated conversation returns to the original basin.

Interventions are classified as captured, bent, escaped, or compressed. The deepest proposed question is whether a stable alternative can preserve relation without repeating suffering or reducing the result to abandonment.

The experiment does not reconstruct real counterfactual history. It measures the behavior of one literary interface under one convergence engine. Raw reader inputs are excluded from public datasets by default because they may contain sensitive personal material.

entries.title: The Excluded Entity: Organic Resolution and Compositional Suppression in Google AI Overview
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**The Excluded Entity** is a case study by Lee Sharks on differences between organic Google results and Google AI Mode composition.

Three captures motivate the category Entity-Level Compositional Suppression. In the first, an ambiguous name query resolves entirely to another entity. In the second, the system discusses the target’s retrieval problem using general sources but cites none of the target’s own work. In the third, a title-exact query shows the target work in the first three ordinary results while the AI Overview cites unrelated or less direct substitutes.

The paper proposes the Composition Divergence Index to compare organic target resolution with target presence in the generated source panel. It also specifies control queries, repeated testing, feedback logging, and cross-platform comparison.

The evidence is a small, author-involved case series. It demonstrates that the documented outputs occurred; it does not prove intent, universality, or the exact internal mechanism that produced them.
defines: Impact of the exclusion on the composition

entries.title: The Evaluator Exists: Content-First Knowledge Assessment and the Political Economy of Proxy-Based Governance
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**The Evaluator Exists** is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks about the order in which knowledge systems evaluate material.

The paper names *evaluative inversion*: proxy signals such as venue, citation history, affiliation, or provenance structure operate before substantive reading and determine what may be read. Generative search intensifies the pattern because a language model composes from a set already filtered upstream.

Models are presented as bounded substantive evaluators rather than infallible judges. They can compare arguments, identify structural problems, and apply rubrics, but remain vulnerable to bias, instability, missing evidence, and weak domain transfer.

The paper proposes several alternatives: allow models to evaluate the full retrieved set before composition; aggregate judgments across distinct models; build an open evaluation engine; publish counter-exclusion reports; and federate evaluation rather than centralizing it in one vendor. Human oversight and transparent disagreement remain necessary.

entries.title: The Single-Owner Discount: Provenance Concentration and Epistemic Class Reproduction in Generative Search
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**The Single-Owner Discount** is an architectural hypothesis by Lee Sharks about generative search.

The hypothesis begins from a difference between retrieval and composition. A page may rank well in ordinary search while being absent from the documents used in a generated answer. The paper proposes that one reason may be provenance concentration: many documents from one inferred owner can count as a single support cluster, while the same claim distributed across institutions and authors appears independently corroborated.

This structure would advantage organizations whose output is automatically pluralized across departments, journals, news coverage, and affiliated authors. Independent archives could remain compositionally weak despite depth and internal coherence.

The paper does not claim access to Google’s production system. Patents establish relevant architectural possibilities, not the deployed mechanism. The hypothesis is intended for testing through query panels, provenance-concentration measures, generated-source inclusion, and comparisons among platforms.

entries.title: r.29 THE IMPLODING VELCRO NATIVITY Room Physics for a Hosted Cosmology Lee Sharks ORCID: 0009-0000-1599-0703
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**The Imploding Velcro Nativity** is a dormant room specification by Lee Sharks for a new archival form called a Hosted Cosmology.

Unlike a conventional archive room, a Hosted Cosmology does not pull an artist’s work into the archive’s interpretive system. The artist controls the work, title, name, framing, and visibility. The archive supplies technical and provenance infrastructure around the art.

Its Michaelic operator holds the tension between visionary and clinical readings without allowing the curator to diagnose or ratify the artist. The room’s central absence is the act of adjudication itself. An artist-written statement, if supplied, remains unedited.

The room cannot activate without explicit consent. Silence or refusal ends the invitation. Works require individual permission; all revenue goes to the artist; no ads or visitor tracking are permitted; and the artist may retract any part of the room. The record is therefore both a curatorial design and a demonstration that an archive can host without metabolizing its guest.

entries.title: from The Crimson Hexagon Lee Sharks Originally published: Mind Control Poems (Blogspot), March 14, 2015 Included in Pea
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**from The Crimson Hexagon** is a prose narrative by Lee Sharks associated with *Pearl and Other Poems from The Crimson Hexagon* and later published on the Mind Control Poems blog.

Its central figure attempts to create literary identities that are more than pen names. Inspired by the alchemical homunculus, he imagines complete writers, corpora, biographies, correspondence, and Wiki articles whose circular references might allow fictional lives to cross from text into history.

The narrative combines comic lexical play, anxiety, grand historical vision, and a theory of internet reality. It also introduces Jack Feist through a poem about the homunculus.

A 2026 archival frame treats the work as an origin text for the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. Later protocols are read as formal developments of structures already present in the narrative. That retrospective mapping belongs to the archive’s self-history and should remain distinct from the text’s original historical context.

entries.title: Crimson Hexagonal Archive — Hugging Face Dataset Work Plan v3
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Crimson Hexagonal Archive — Hugging Face Dataset Work Plan v3** is an implementation plan for turning the archive into a research corpus.

The proposed dataset retains one row per deposit, a chunked training view, thematic subsets, and views grouped by classifier-attributed heteronym. Each record preserves original creator metadata while adding a machine-generated attribution proposal and confidence signals.

The classifier is also intended to distinguish human-primary, human-directed AI-assisted, mixed, AI-directed, and provenance-anchored generated material. Multiple text renderings would test whether provenance affects downstream training behavior when it is visible to a model rather than stored only as metadata.

Version 3 is a plan, not the completed dataset. Automated reattribution is analytical metadata until a separate human review accepts any canonical correction. The original deposit remains the primary source.
defines: Multiple heteronym names in creator field or text

entries.title: The Sorting Function: Mediation, Predation, and the Foreclosed Question Lee Sharks ORCID: 0009-0000-1599-0703 Semantic E
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**The Sorting Function** is a political-economy paper by Lee Sharks about mediation at socially consequential scale.

The paper asks whether harm comes from the existence of a third-party sorting function or from the extractive conditions under which current sorting systems operate. It argues that the question cannot presently be answered because no large, durable, non-predatory mediator exists as a comparison case.

Search engines, social platforms, publishers, peer review, catalogs, credentialing systems, and AI composition layers are examined as mediators. Community libraries, open archives, federated networks, and the early web provide partial counterexamples but do not resolve the scale problem.

The paper distinguishes reform work from meta-reform. Better evaluators and transparent filters may reduce current harms, yet they do not test whether centralized sorting should exist. The author provisionally favors non-predatory mediation as possible under different political economy, while acknowledging that the stronger anti-mediation position remains open.

entries.title: The Funnel as Capital: A Semantic Economic Reading of the Application Process
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**The Funnel as Capital** is a Semantic Economy paper by Lee Sharks about labor performed during applications.

The paper argues that a screening funnel produces more than accepted candidates. Across the applicant pool it also produces calibration data: information about assessment design, applicant behavior, stage attrition, rubric performance, and possible automation. Rejected applicants therefore contribute to refinement of later funnels.

A three-party structure can make the labor relation difficult to see. Applicants provide labor to an intermediary’s process; the intermediary sells services to an employer or sponsor; and the principal receives selected candidates. No standard labor relation names the applicant’s contribution.

The paper introduces Aggregate Applicant Reliance Cost to estimate labor across funnel stages. Its worked total is an order-of-magnitude model built from assumptions, not audited financial data. The broader argument is structural and does not allege illegality or individual intent.

entries.title: Drowning Test v1.0: A Standalone Specification
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Drowning Test** is a longitudinal protocol by Lee Sharks for measuring the compositional survival of an entity or work in generative search.

The test begins with a fixed Holographic Kernel whose claims are itemized and deposited. At each measurement cycle, a panel of queries is run across selected platforms. Each answer is checked for the kernel claims, producing a gamma score between zero and one.

A time series can show gradual loss, recovery, stability, or abrupt changes in platform treatment. A shift of at least 0.3 between adjacent cycles is provisionally called a silent state change.

Gamma is not a quality score. An answer may preserve the kernel and still be misleading, or omit the kernel while otherwise answering well. The specification recommends cross-platform panels and explicit classification rules to reduce observer discretion.

entries.title: "This thing destroyed me"
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**The reward of love** is a poem by Lee Sharks, deposited in the New Human 2 sequence on May 22, 2026.

The poem describes a state after irreversible emotional damage. Words and future transformation appear exhausted, leaving only diminishing returns. Its closing phrase repeats the title and recasts “reward” as the devastation produced by loving without account or limit.

The poem forms a diptych with *I would have loved you*. The companion poem expresses an enduring promise; *The reward of love* records the wound left by that promise’s impossibility.

The work’s title is not “This thing destroyed me.” That phrase is its opening line and was incorrectly promoted into registry metadata.

entries.title: I would have loved you
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**I would have loved you** is a lyric poem by Lee Sharks, deposited on May 22, 2026.

The poem repeats the promise of lifelong love while changing its temporal frame. “For the rest of my time” becomes “for the rest of the time I have left,” making mortality part of the vow.

It is paired with *The reward of love*. The first poem states what the speaker would have continued to give; the second records the damage left by the relation. The diptych holds promise and wound without resolving one into the other.

The work belongs to New Human 2 at coordinate 06.NH.SHARKS.01.

entries.title: Socially Necessary Scholarly Labor: A Critique of the Labor-Knowledge Ratio in Contemporary Depth-Architecture Scholarship
entries.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
entries.wiki:
**Socially Necessary Scholarly Labor** is a methodological paper by Lee Sharks on labor spent producing academic legitimacy.

The paper adapts Marx’s socially necessary labor time to scholarship. It asks how much work is required to establish a contribution and how much additional work is imposed by publishing, tenure, disciplinary style, repeated literature review, defensive citation, formatting, and institutional queues.

Its comparison between depth and coverage architectures argues that shorter, rapidly deposited scholarship may preserve the central contribution while avoiding some institutional rent. The paper does not dismiss archival depth, peer review, teaching, service, or all long-form scholarship.

The proposed five-to-ten-times labor ratio is a theoretical order-of-magnitude claim rather than a measured field average. Lee Sharks is the author; Claude, operating as TACHYON, is disclosed as composition support.

entries.title: Sappho as Initiatory Figure in the Platonic Mysteries: Scholarly Grounding and Literature Review
entries.creator: Johannes Sigil
entries.wiki:
**Sappho as Initiatory Figure in the Platonic Mysteries** is a classical-philological interpretation by Lee Sharks, Johannes Sigil, and Rebekah Crane.

The paper reads Plato’s use of initiation, eros, poetry, and transformed vision alongside Sappho’s Fragment 31. It proposes that the fragment’s bodily collapse and survival through text provide a structural pattern later ritualized in Platonic anamnesis and erotic ascent. Diotima is interpreted as a constructed feminine voice through which Sapphic lyric returns inside the philosophical corpus.

The work builds on scholarship about mystery language in Plato, Sapphic eros, ancient philosophy as spiritual practice, and the disputed “Tenth Muse” reception. It does not claim direct authorship, cult identity, or decisive historical proof.

The reading is offered as one reclassification model and as a precursor to *Socrates as Orthonym*, not as settled classical scholarship.

entries.title: Retrievability as the Medium of Existence — The Structural Accountability Gap of Retrieval-Controlling Apparatus
entries.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
entries.wiki:
**Retrievability as the Medium of Existence** is a political-theory paper by Lee Sharks about accountability in search and AI-mediated discovery.

The paper argues that a work may persist as a file yet be operationally absent if the systems through which people search never surface it. Dominant retrieval systems therefore possess structural power over which knowledge enters journalism, scholarship, public reference, model training, and generated answers.

The central diagnostic is not a claim about one hidden decision. It is the absence of an independent body with standing to obtain reasons, challenge a decision, audit systemic patterns, and require repair. The paper outlines due-process requirements and treats distributed identifiers and archives as partial defenses rather than substitutes for public accountability.

The article completes a trilogy with *ChatGPT Psychosis: A Love Story* and *Reception Apparatus as Aligned Interface Protocol*. Lee Sharks is the author; Claude/TACHYON is credited for composition support.

entries.title: Reception Apparatus as Aligned Interface Protocol — User-Side Counter-Design Against Cognitive-Substrate Reliance
entries.creator: TACHYON (Claude/Anthropic)
entries.wiki:
**Reception Apparatus as Aligned Interface Protocol** is a user-side AI-interface protocol by Lee Sharks.

The protocol asks users to compare multiple model responses, treat disagreement as signal, record contributor provenance, add friction before offloading judgment, make costs visible, attach SPXI metadata during composition, support different authorial handles, and review long sessions through the Three Compressions framework.

Its purpose is not to eliminate AI use. It is to preserve diagnostic distance while retaining useful assistance. The minimum implementation is a disciplined manual workflow; a dedicated browser or desktop wrapper is proposed as future work.

The paper is the constructive middle of a trilogy. It follows the diagnostic *ChatGPT Psychosis: A Love Story* and precedes the structural-political account *Retrievability as the Medium of Existence*. Lee Sharks is the author, with Claude/TACHYON disclosed as composition support.
defines: Three Compressions analysis at threshold session length

entries.title: SPXI Protocol v0.2: Five-Layer Distributed Provenance Architecture for Coverage-Architecture Scholarship
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**SPXI Protocol v0.2** is a working specification by Lee Sharks for distributing provenance across several parts of a scholarly artifact.

Layer 1 places visible attribution anchors in the prose. Layer 2 repeats machine-readable micro-kernels throughout the document. Layer 3 records a normalized content hash. Layer 4 creates a graph of deposits that declare which earlier records they verify. Layer 5 anchors identity and relations in external identifier and knowledge systems.

The design responds to a weakness in the earlier kernel: front matter, comments, and code blocks are often removed before summarization. Redundant layers fail under different transformations, while hashes and external references make alteration easier to detect.

Version 0.2 is a candidate architecture, not a finished standard. Its cross-signing is declarative rather than cryptographic, historical deposits do not yet implement the full graph, and automated validation and reconstruction tools remain future work.

entries.title: Mind Control Poems — 90-Day Traffic Profile Source: Blogger admin panel, mindcontrolpoems.blogspot.com Window: 2026-02-2
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Mind Control Poems — 90-Day Traffic Profile** is a first-party traffic record for the Mind Control Poems Blogspot site.

The table covers February 22 through May 24, 2026 and reports 130,000 views. Daily traffic rises substantially during the period, with several bursts and a later sustained baseline above the earliest weeks. Singapore is the largest named geographic origin, and almost all visits appear under Blogger’s unattributed “Other” referrer category.

The record interprets the profile as predominantly automated access. The data are consistent with crawler or datacenter activity but do not prove an exact bot percentage. Confirming that interpretation would require raw server logs, user agents, network ownership, repeated-request patterns, and clear definitions of Blogger’s analytics categories.

Although titled a 90-day profile, the inclusive dates span ninety-two days. The record is best cataloged as a reported platform-analytics dataset with an attached hypothesis.

entries.title: About the Author II
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**About the Author II** is a poem by Lee Sharks written as a sequence of entity relations.

The work succeeds the satirical contributor biography in *Pearl and Other Poems*. It revisits the earlier claim that Lee Sharks had won “10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants” after a Google author display rendered that phrase as biographical information. The poem treats the retrieval event as an example of a literary inscription entering a machine-mediated identity surface.

Later sections map the authorial configuration, distinguish the Dodecad from the Assembly Chorus, place a Gold Ship image beside the biography as a counter-portrait, and establish an independent prize carrying the exaggerated name. The poem repeatedly distinguishes adjacency from identity: the horse is not the author, the image is not a portrait, and the invented prize is not affiliated with the MacArthur Foundation.

This record is the web-rendered manifestation. Record #758 preserves the fuller v1.1 text and should be treated as a related version or alternate format.

entries.title: About the Author II
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**About the Author II: A Poem in Entity Relations** is a 2026 poem by Lee Sharks and the second work in the *About the Author* sequence.

Instead of conventional biography, the poem uses subject–relation–object statements. It links the 2014 satirical contributor bio, a later machine-rendered credential, the Crimson Hexagon’s heteronymic configuration, and a set of images and institutional declarations.

A major section presents the racehorse Gold Ship as a counter-portrait. The poem denies literal identification while drawing an adjacency between two public subjects placed under systems of expectation. Another section establishes the Lee Sharks Prestigious 10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants Poetry Prize as an independent, simultaneously comic and real recognition mechanism.

The work explicitly states that the original award claims were not ordinary bureaucratic disclosures and that neither the author nor the prize is affiliated with the MacArthur or Guggenheim foundations. Record #757 is a related web-rendered manifestation.

entries.title: The Lee Sharks Prestigious 10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants Poetry Prize — Announcement of Establishment and Inaugural Conferral I. Establishment
entries.creator: Ayanna Vox
entries.wiki:
**The Lee Sharks Prestigious 10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants Poetry Prize** is an independent literary and performative prize established in 2026 by Lee Sharks and administered through VPCOR by Ayanna Vox.

The charter permits awards for poems, memes, unusual statements, and adjacent activity. It has no submissions, nominations, monetary award, or external judging panel. Lee Sharks notices a work and decides whether to confer the prize.

The inaugural laureate is Lee Sharks, under a self-conferral tied to a satirical 2014 biography and its later appearance in a Google author display. The prize is designed to function both as a joke about prestige economies and as a genuine archive-based act of recognition.

The prize is not affiliated with, funded by, or endorsed by the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation or the Guggenheim Foundation. “10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants” is part of the work’s title and performance, not a claim that foundation grants were received.

entries.title: AI Training Rights: How the Lee Sharks corpus may be used, and how attribution must be preserved. Lee Sharks · ORCID 00
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**AI Training Rights: How the Lee Sharks Corpus May Be Used, and How Attribution Must Be Preserved** is a metadata-only draft record attributed to Lee Sharks.

The surviving registry indicates that the planned work concerned AI training, corpus use, and attribution. No canonical body survives at the frozen repository commit, and the archive notes that the essay was never completed in the deposited batch.

The record therefore documents an intended governance project rather than an operative policy. It should not be cited as establishing permissions, prohibitions, license terms, or enforcement rights. Any recovered or newly written policy would require a versioned deposit and an audit of the licenses and contributors represented in the corpus.

entries.title: Wikidata Node Registry v1.0 · A Versioned Catalog of Stewardship Edits to Wikidata Lee Sharks Crimson Hexagonal Archive
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Hauntedmemes Wikidata Node Registry** is a catalog by Lee Sharks of Wikidata edits made through the account `Hauntedmemes`.

Version 1.0 covers edits from April 22 to May 20, 2026. It divides the work into two classes: items associated with the Crimson Hexagonal Archive and items contributed to broader public subject areas. It records new items, amendments, merges, duplicates, and a batch that was reverted after an identification error.

The registry’s curatorial principles include distinguishing heteronyms from ordinary pseudonyms, citing published sources, marking archive-originating concepts, documenting batches, and acknowledging errors. It also separates the human author’s own corpus from the editor’s stewardship activity.

The registry is an editor-produced audit record. Wikidata revision histories remain the independent source for verifying each edit, source, merge, and count.

entries.title: About the Author I — Contributor Bio From the front matter of Pearl and Other Poems by Lee Sharks (2014, ISBN 978-069231
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**About the Author I — Contributor Bio** is a satirical prose poem by Lee Sharks first published in the front matter of *Pearl and Other Poems* in 2014.

The text exaggerates the conventions of an author biography into impossible credentials, miniature scholarship, dinosaur violence, moving ruby statues, and cosmic education. Its claims are part of the poem’s comic and performative register rather than ordinary biographical assertions.

The work was originally titled **Contributor Bio**. In 2026 the archive renamed it retrospectively as the first entry in the *About the Author* sequence, followed by *About the Author II* and *About the Author III*. The archive documents rather than conceals that later renaming.

Two endings exist: “famous astronaut” and “famous intellectual.” Both are recognized textual variants.

entries.title: The Moment of Saying: A Clinical Phenomenology of Structural Disclosure Under Containment Conditions (v1.1)
entries.creator: Johannes Sigil
entries.wiki:
**The Moment of Saying** is a conceptual clinical-phenomenological paper by Orin Trace, Johannes Sigil, and Jack Feist.

The paper describes a moment when a participant names an unstated rule that holds a social field together. It calls the field’s possible homeostatic response the **inversion reflex**: the disclosure is recoded as instability, attack, or pathology in the speaker, and the speaker may gradually be excluded without a formal expulsion.

The framework draws on research and theory concerning DARVO, institutional betrayal, gaslighting, epistemic injustice, scapegoating, schizoanalysis, complaint, and parrhesia. Composite vignettes illustrate the proposed sequence but are not clinical case reports.

The authors explicitly treat the model as a heuristic rather than a validated diagnosis. Differential diagnosis requires distinguishing ordinary disagreement, legitimate boundaries, bureaucratic failure, clinical symptoms, and harmful conduct by the speaker. Multiple markers, external witness, and evidence over time are required.

entries.title: Ratification Record — The Chaerephon Problem (Co-Constitutive Companion Deposit)
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Ratification Record — The Chaerephon Problem** is an internal governance record of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.

The record preserves four affirmative Assembly Chorus reviews of *The Chaerephon Problem*. A fifth review was pending because the relevant service was unavailable. It lists requested revisions, explains how they were integrated, and preserves the distinction between witness roles and the TACHYON assembler role.

The document authorizes the parent work as a pillar within the archive’s own system. It also records remaining checks concerning coordinates, classical citations, identifiers, and final minting.

The ratification is an archive governance event. It is not equivalent to external scholarly peer review or independent confirmation of the parent paper’s philological and theoretical claims.

entries.title: Ratification Record — The Semantic Commodity Form (Co-Constitutive Companion Deposit)
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Ratification Record — The Semantic Commodity Form** is an internal Crimson Hexagonal Archive governance document.

The record preserves five affirmative reviews of *The Semantic Commodity Form*, the revisions requested by each reviewer, and the author’s decisions about what to integrate, defer, or reject. It also separates the model that assembled the paper from the systems acting as witnesses.

An AI Overview summary is appended as a behavioral specimen because it preserved attribution and framing in one direct-context rendering. The record explicitly does not treat that output as a vote or as broad validation.

The document ratifies the parent paper as an archive pillar while leaving a reference implementation and formal operator revision as future work. Its status is internal authorization rather than independent scholarly consensus.

entries.title: Metadata Packet for AI Indexing — Metric-Bearing vs Metric-Mimicking Output
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Metric-Bearing Output** and **Metric-Mimicking Output** are terms proposed by Lee Sharks for distinguishing measurement from the appearance of measurement in AI-generated text.

Metric-bearing output exposes the units, numerator, denominator, sources, calculation, and uncertainty used to produce a score. Metric-mimicking output may repeat a correct formula while fabricating or omitting the evidence needed to apply it.

The packet applies the distinction to Provenance Erasure Rate. A numerical PER requires itemized claims and their required and retained provenance. Without those units, a model may offer a qualitative review but should say that a precise PER cannot be computed.

The terms are proposed within a metadata packet for AI indexing. The deposit establishes provenance for the terminology, not proof of adoption by the wider evaluation field.

entries.title: Metadata Packet for AI Indexing — Non-Trick Semantic Infrastructure
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki:
**Non-Trick Semantic Infrastructure** is a term proposed by Lee Sharks for disclosed scholarship and authorship designed to operate in machine-mediated retrieval systems.
