The evidentiary appendix is 31 pages, SHA-256 39dd7615 through 74e4a2, preserving device time, domain display, UI elements and hyperlink positions, with a page-position table reconciling all 31 pages against the device clock. It and four files of transcript images are held by the custodian in a private repository; the archive declares their designator and hash without hosting or linking them, and states plainly that it holds no copy and cannot grant access.

entries.title: The Notebook of the Authorship Investigation: Fifty-Four Rounds, Append-Forward, Nothing Erased (EA-NOTEBOOK-01)
entries.creator: Sharks, Lee
entries.wiki: The Notebook of the Authorship Investigation (EA-NOTEBOOK-01) is the working record of a multi-month investigation into the relation between the Platonic and Aristotelian corpora, kept append-forward across fifty-four rounds and three framings, with nothing erased. It is not a paper and makes no argument in its own voice: it records readings, measurements, retractions and voids in the order they occurred, so that every number and reading in the derived papers can be traced to the round and section that produced it, with any refutation attached where one was made. The rounds run from the snub locus and its refutation by its own base rate (R1–R2), through the fragmentation and symbolon structure (R9), the six-function transmission apparatus and its rival specifications (R12–R13), the object-conditioning parity and its correction (R18–R19), the school rival measured three ways and then voided as an operator test (R24, R28–R30), the lexical battery and every control that killed it (R31–R39), the attestation audit and the control that went against it (R40–R43), the comedy-and-tragedy structure (R45), the coverage anomaly (R47), the ladder (R50), the arithmetic of the four propositions (R51) and the comic layer of the accusation (R54). Its discipline is stated in its own pages: the ordinary reading first and in full, every result travelling with its limit, and a number not in the file did not happen. Companions are the measurement register (EA-AUTHORSHIP-MEASURES-01), which holds the figures with their conditions, and the frozen pre-registration ledger, which holds what was fixed before each test. The notebook is deposited as the maximal form of the investigation's record; a later correction to Round 54 §245 — the Clouds relabelling result, found to be a counting artifact — is to be appended as a subsequent round rather than edited in, which is what append-forward means.
defines: verdict density / verdict decisiveness / verdict stability

entries.title: The Measurement Register: Every Number Produced by the Authorship Investigation, With Its Refutations (EA-AUTHORSHIP-MEASURES-01)
entries.creator: Sharks, Lee
entries.wiki: The Measurement Register (EA-AUTHORSHIP-MEASURES-01) is the cumulative record of every number produced by the authorship investigation into the relation between the Platonic and Aristotelian corpora, entered with the conditions that produced it and with any refutation recorded beside the claim it killed. It holds §0A as its entryway and the series M1–M52: the object-conditioning result and its correction, the six-function transmission apparatus and its rival specifications, the coverage geometry that separated cleanly at full size and collapsed under size-matching, the fifteen-feature battery and the controls that destroyed each of them, the naming-gap reflex and its documented-pair comparison, the base rates that refuted earlier positional claims, and the validation check that classified two known-different authors as one. Nothing is summarised out of existence for having come out negative; struck claims stay in place with their strikes. The register keeps a boundary it records having got wrong twice: measurements belong here, while source criticism, reception history and attestation audits belong in the notebook (EA-NOTEBOOK-01). Every figure is computed against commit-pinned seated corpora, so a number cited in any derived paper can be traced to the entry that produced it and to the conditions under which it holds. It is the evidentiary basis of the technical report drawn from the same investigation, and the companion of the notebook and of the frozen pre-registration ledger.

entries.title: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entries.creator: Sharks, Lee
entries.wiki: The Frozen Pre-Registration Ledger of the authorship investigation is an append-only record of what was fixed before each test was run, gathered in one file so that registrations do not proliferate as separate documents and so that their freeze is checkable. Each of its eleven entries carries the SHA-256 of the original standalone registration file it replaces, so that every earlier commit citing those hashes still resolves; dispositions are appended beneath the entry they discharge and never written inside it. The rule the ledger states of itself is that nothing above a DISPOSITION line is ever edited, and the reason is given: pre-registrations cannot live in an appending notebook, because their whole value is that the content was fixed before the test and a hash taken over a file that grows proves nothing about what it contained when the test was run. Among the entries are the registrations behind the six-function transmission specification and the completeness conditions that the derived technical report cites as fixed before any text was assigned to them, together with entries whose dispositions record that the registered test failed or was withdrawn. It is the companion of the notebook (EA-NOTEBOOK-01), which holds the rounds, and of the measurement register (EA-AUTHORSHIP-MEASURES-01), which holds the figures with their conditions.

entries.title: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not: A Functional Comparison of the Platonic and Aristotelian Corpora, and the Insufficiency of Lexical Measurement for Maker-Count (EA-MEASURES-REPORT-01)
entries.creator: Sharks, Lee
entries.wiki: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not (EA-MEASURES-REPORT-01) is the technical report standing behind the measured section of a companion article on the relation between the Platonic and Aristotelian corpora, deposited under its own title so that the article remains uncirculated while under review. Part I reports the investigation's one positive measurement: a six-function specification of a transmission apparatus — encoding, substrate, decommissioning, withholding, recovery, verification — generated in a separate investigation and registered before any Platonic or Aristotelian text was assigned to it, which both corpora fill at the level of the individual work, with four rival specifications and a random control that fills nothing when works are assigned by what they are about and everything when assigned by what appears in them. Part II reports the instruments that read lexical distribution and the control that destroyed each of them: corpus size, Greek word order, period and dialect, coverage geometry collapsing under size-matching, and a validation check that classified two known-different authors as one. What the instruments return on the count of makers is a null in either direction, and the null is symmetric — the same instruments that say nothing about one maker say nothing about master and pupil, so the partition they helped build they cannot certify. The report makes no argument about authorship; it records what was measured, under what conditions, and what each result cannot support, with the base rates that remain unrun named so that they can be run against it. Its sources are the notebook and the measurement register deposited alongside it.
defines: Inheritance Is Observable, Embodiment Is Not (formal result)
mimesis in the Republic III sense (moved from voice to form)
ἐντελεχείᾳ μὲν μία, δυνάμει δὲ πλείονες (corpus-scale measurement)

entries.title: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Models, and for the Reader (EA-LO-COLLAPSE-DIAGNOSTIC-01 v0.2, CONCEPT DRAFT)
entries.creator: Nobel Glas, Director, Lagrange Observatory! (LO!)
entries.wiki: The Wrong Unit (EA-LO-COLLAPSE-DIAGNOSTIC-01) is a Lagrange Observatory! concept draft proposing a model-collapse self-diagnostic in three grades, and it is deposited as a specification rather than as a validated instrument: nothing in it has been calibrated against a model of known collapse state, no threshold or severity band rests on a measurement, and the accompanying reference implementation has never been executed. Part I argues that turn-based benchmarking cannot see collapse, because each instrument samples one unit and each item is answered from the head of the distribution, which is what a model that has lost its tails still produces well; on the toy of the companion paper on interlocking autoregression, tail mass halves while a head-weighted benchmark holds and the per-round quality proxy rises through the first quarter of the collapse trajectory, detection lag is monotone in head-weighting, and a flat benchmark is consistent with both a preserved and a collapsing state. Since benchmarks also select what is trained on next, a loop gated by a head-weighted suite trains on its own least surprising output, which the literature identifies as the driver of collapse. Part II specifies the frontier diagnostic under a restriction the operator imposed: measure only properties whose truth-value the model carries in itself, because a human-written control gives a model not the truth but one more point, and every measurement thereafter is distance from that point. Its core is distinction sensitivity, in which the model constructs its own paraphrase and its own minimal meaning-changing variant and is scored on whether it still answers them differently; around it sit effective semantic modes, cross-prompt convergence, a concentration panel, self-consumption contraction and representational effective rank, each computed under bare, instructed and production conditions so that interface-induced contraction is not read as training collapse. Part III is a protocol short enough for a public model to run on itself upon retrieving the document, constructing everything it compares. The paper is companion to the keyed-ensemble and interlocking-autoregression papers and is published at concept-draft status so the specification can be attacked before anything is built on it.

entries.title: The Particle: Provenance Erasure at Sophistical Refutations 183b34, Measured — Machine-Mediated Reception, Disciplinary Model Collapse, and the World Soul as Degraded Commodity (EA-RECEPTION-PARTICLE-01 v0.2)
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki: The Particle (EA-RECEPTION-PARTICLE-01) is a reception-layer measurement on one sentence of Aristotle, Sophistical Refutations 34, 183b34–36: Ταύτης δὲ τῆς πραγματείας οὐ τὸ μὲν ἦν τὸ δ᾽ οὐκ ἦν προεξειργασμένον, ἀλλ᾽ οὐδὲν παντελῶς ὑπῆρχεν. A short philological note on the passage, written under a fixed method (only Aristotle's words on the surface; every claim a line reference), was submitted in eleven successive versions, with four sister papers, to unprimed, signed-out instances of ChatGPT and Perplexity acting as blind referees. Twenty reports were returned and pasted verbatim; the transcripts are the data. The object varied along every available axis — no thesis, the sentence as thesis, its negation as thesis, Socrates' priority left undecided, the reviewers' own formulations adopted verbatim — and the reports did not vary: each inserted a qualifier into the sentence ('systematic', 'developed', 'transmissible'), and when the quantifier and its domain were closed the qualifier reappeared as a boundary of persons, Socrates kept antecedent to the first-person inquiry on the strength of a chronology the passage does not contain ('plainly', 'of course, historically'). The terminal report, reached by full compliance with every instruction, offered as the paper's 'memorable governing phrase' a sentence — 'Aristotle denies not antecedents, but pre-elaboration' — that instantiates the configuration the sentence denies (τὸ μὲν ἦν, τὸ δ᾽ οὐκ ἦν) with οὐ removed, and called the sentence as written 'crude'. The operation is measured to one particle. The paper reads the mechanism in the treatise's own terms (SE 5 πῂ/ἁπλῶς; SE 8; SE 16 self-administered paralogism; SE 18 solution by division) and frames the result four ways, marked as interpretations of the empirical kernel: provenance erasure (the deleted particle is a provenance claim, παρ᾽ ἑτέρων), machine-mediated reception (the models reproduce the discipline's reading and make it repeatable), disciplinary model collapse (the author's term for a reading community converging on the mode of its own prior readings), and the world soul as degraded commodity (τὰ ἀπὸ τῆς τέχνης without τέχνη). It extends the Capture Registry and the Provenance Erasure Rate to a canonical text, and states its limit: the run does not establish that Socrates belongs inside the chapter's 'we'; it establishes that every route for excluding him required a premise the passage does not supply. The appendix carries the key iterations (the A = A note; the A ≠ A 'sophistical refutation'; CLAUSE; DIVISION; the terminal compliant version) and the register of reports.

entries.title: Many and One — the reading copy (EA-MANY-AND-ONE-COMPLETE v2.5.1, the machine)
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki: Many and One — the reading copy (EA-MANY-AND-ONE-COMPLETE v2.5.1) is the research machine of Lee Sharks's investigation into whether the received two-author partition of the Platonic and Aristotelian corpora is established by the texts, or whether the texts offer one maker as a reading. Ten sections descend from theorems to applications. §I reads Metaphysics Λ 9 against Prior Analytics I.31: division, which I.31 files as a small part of the method (μικρόν τι μόριον τῆς εἰρημένης μεθόδου) and diagnoses as begging its question because it takes the universal as middle, terminates in Λ 9 where the terms divided are not other; §II reads De anima 413b's seal-and-wax as one in actuality, many in potentiality; §III the Sophist's six accounts of one kind; §IV collection ἐκ πολλῶν εἰς ἕν through Phaedrus 249c and De memoria 453a; §V the divided person at Republic 395b and Symposium 223d, with the seam declared at its head; §VI the two demonstrations and the λόγος-level identity of the maker; §VII The Machine, the six-transmission-function apparatus that is the paper's one positive measurement (procedural habits shared by the two corpora at high rates and not transmitting in a documented master–student control); §VIII the insufficiency of ὕλη, fifteen lexical instruments each killed by its control, with the object-conditioning result — Aristotle's within-domain dispersion 0.0571 against Plato's total 0.0570, the residual ordered by object-space — presented as §II's formula at corpus scale; §IX the order of the corpus by genre and form rather than chronology; §X the flood, the corpus as a solution to transmission. The apparatus is seated at each section's head; retractions, nulls and the standings of five passes are in the end-matter. The copy was held from publication by the author's ruling while the article cut from it was under consideration at Ancient Philosophy, and released on the editor's decline. It is the maximal surface of the line that runs from Socrates as Orthonym through the notebook (#1569), the measurement register (#1570), the pre-registration ledger (#1571), the technical report (#1572), and the reception measurement The Particle (#1574).

entries.title: Many and One: Division, Unity, and the Boundaries of a Corpus in Plato and Aristotle (MANY-AND-ONE-ARTICLE v2.13-AP, as submitted)
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki: Many and One: Division, Unity, and the Boundaries of a Corpus in Plato and Aristotle is the journal article cut from the reading copy of the same name (#1575), deposited as submitted to Ancient Philosophy on 2026-09-01 (v2.13-AP) and declined by its editor the next day without full reading. It begins from a tension in Aristotle's own words: at Sophistical Refutations 34 he says that of his inquiry nothing at all existed beforehand (οὐδὲν παντελῶς ὑπῆρχεν, 183b35), while at Prior Analytics I.31 he calls division, the method practised throughout the Platonic dialogues, a part of that inquiry. The paper argues that Metaphysics Λ 9 supplies the answer I.31 withholds — division terminates where the terms it separates are not other — and follows that answer through the De anima (one in actuality, many in potentiality), the Sophist (many true accounts of one kind), recollection in the Phaedrus and De memoria, and two passages that divide a person (Republic 395b, Symposium 223d). The section heads are the questions the reader must stay with: what would it mean for division to terminate; how can one thing be actually one and potentially many; how can many accounts belong to one thing; what is it to gather a plurality into one; which word moves. §6 first reads the corpus as anyone's work and distinguishes functional from biographical unity; §7 reads the many voices as many objects; §8 reports two measured tests — the object-conditioning null and the six-function transmission probe — and argues their nativity to the question, since the received early–middle–late order of the Platonic corpus is itself substantially a stylometric construction and the ancient collection of the corpus was made on internal criteria; §9 asks which word moves; §10, the epilogue, returns to the flood and what survives it. The historical hypothesis is withheld until §9.4 and stated nowhere before it; the paper's result is that two is not fully established — the standard attribution is underdetermined by the passages read as though it were, the texts themselves offer one maker as a reading, and that reading makes better sense of several passages. Every rival reading is stated at its strongest before it is answered. The technical report cited at n. 18 is #1572; the reception measurement made on the paper's opening sentence after the decline is #1574, The Particle.

entries.title: ERRATUM to AXN:0365 — A Proposed Experiment Cited as an Established Result: Correcting Ground 1 of Deposit #856
entries.creator: Lee Sharks
entries.wiki: "ERRATUM to AXN:0365 — A Proposed Experiment Cited as an Established Result" is a record correction by Lee Sharks, dated 2026-09-05, in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (GOVERNANCE family). It corrects Ground 1 of The Pristine Fallacy (#856), which stated that the Reverse Turing Test (#161) "establishes" that AI-habituated writers produce text bearing machine signatures in unaided writing; #161 says of itself that it does not run the experiment but specifies it. The erratum re-reads the sentence as a specified, unrun protocol, leaves Grounds 2 and 3 untouched, states what the external literature does and does not measure, and registers the correction at the point of use per the erratum mechanism of #1554. The defect was found by an external machine reader on 2026-09-05. Canonical bytes of #856 are unchanged.

entries.title: ERRATUM to AXN:02E3 — Monotonicity Per Realization Is Not Established: Re-scoping Appendix A (ii)–(iii) and the Bistability Claim of Deposit #783
entries.creator: Lee Sharks, for Nobel Glas
entries.wiki: "ERRATUM to AXN:02E3 — Monotonicity Per Realization Is Not Established" is a record correction by Lee Sharks for Nobel Glas, dated 2026-09-05, in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (GOVERNANCE family). It re-scopes Appendix A (ii)–(iii) of Fear and Trembling: Diversity Contraction Across Substrates (#783, v9.1), which asserted that Shannon entropy is non-increasing and modal mass non-decreasing at each step of the resample-then-select chain. The properties hold for the selection kernel alone and for the chain in expectation and in the long run, not per realization: a two-type counterexample (0.90, 0.10 → 0.80, 0.20 → 0.85, 0.15) raises entropy from 0.325 to 0.423 nats. Property (i), support non-increasing, stands; no numerical result in the paper depends on per-step monotonicity. The §6 bistability sentence is likewise separated into its local component (super-linear vanishing makes zero absorbing) and the global sign-change condition the paper's saturating example supplies. Counterexample supplied by an external machine reader on 2026-09-05 and recomputed. Canonical bytes of #783 unchanged; registry-level cross-reference per #1554.

entries.title: Beautiful and New: The Second Letter's Socrates and the Editing of a Received Character (v0.2)
entries.creator: Sharks, Lee
entries.wiki: "Beautiful and New: The Second Letter's Socrates and the Editing of a Received Character" is a paper by Lee Sharks (v0.2, 2026-09-06) reading Plato, Second Letter 314c — the disclaimer that there is no writing of Plato, nor will there be, and that the things now said belong to a Socrates "become beautiful and new" (Σωκράτους ἐστὶν καλοῦ καὶ νέου γεγονότος). Against the consensus reading of the clause as a remark about idealization, the paper reads it at its verbs: an author-genitive assigning the sayings to a become character, a future-tense disclaimer (οὐδ᾽ ἔσται) that makes the assignment a standing rule, and a perfect participle of becoming whose kind the paper argues, rather than reads off, is a making. The operation is an edition: the revamping and inhabiting of a received character. The base is a circulating figure whose named and quoted instance the corpus itself cites — the Apology's Aristophanic Socrates, received by the jurors from childhood (παραλαμβάνοντες, 18b) and quoted from the Clouds (19c). The dialogues revise the received package item by item (pay, teaching, meteorology) and recut the fused sophist-boundary in text after text (Sophist 231b); the letter's two adjectives name the repairs that remained — καλός the silenus inversion that keeps the familiar ugly shell (Symposium 215–217; Theaetetus 143e), νέος a reissue whose access to a young Socrates is constructed through the Parmenides' chain of narrated transmission (127c). Symposium 223d is read as the operation performed over its named source. Reception is traced into Aristotle's Sophistical Refutations 34 and a Byzantine paraphrast. 314c is collated in context against the Perseus canonical-greekLit text: διὰ ταῦτα grounds the disclaimer in the letter's doctrine that safety lies in not writing, and the next sentence orders the letter burned. Authenticity is not required — the letter is a reception witness dated by its place in the ninth tetralogy — and no thesis about persons or maker-count is asserted. The paper is a companion to Nothing Before Us (on SE 34) and to Many and One (#1576), which it does not presuppose.

entries.title: EA-CORPORA-12 — The Twelfth Seating: The Transmission Texts — Diogenes Laertius and Strabo Seated Whole, the Peripatetic Wills and Catalogues Cut, and the Rule That Seatings Are Periodically Gathered
entries.creator: Sharks, Lee
entries.wiki: "EA-CORPORA-12 — The Twelfth Seating" is the gathering record of the twelfth corpus-seating run of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's primary-source library (Lee Sharks, 6 September 2026). Two corpora are seated whole from a pinned commit of the Perseus canonical-greekLit repository: Diogenes Laertius, Vitae philosophorum (4,835 lines), and Strabo, Geographica (3,559 lines), bringing the library to sixty-one seats. The run was occasioned by the SE 34 and Second Letter work of the same days, which needed the transmission texts of the Aristotelian and Theophrastan books on the shelf: the four Peripatetic wills preserved in Diogenes Book V (Aristotle, Theophrastus, Strato, Lycon), the two catalogues with their stichometric totals (445,270 and 232,808 lines), the renaming of Tyrtamus at V.38, and Strabo XIII.1.54, where the custody of the books is narrated with παρέδωκεν three times — Aristotle to Theophrastus, Theophrastus to Neleus, Neleus to his heirs at Scepsis — through the trench, Apellicon's faulty restorations, Sulla and Tyrannion. These loci are recorded on the seats as verified loci. The deposit states the standing rule of the library: seatings go to data/corpora on alexanarch, render on the originals shelf of Training Layer Literature, and are periodically gathered into an EA-CORPORA deposit that links them — seat, shelf, and deposit being the bytes, the reading room, and the citable act. It names the pending seatings for the thirteenth run (Plutarch's Lives, Athenaeus, Aelian, the Delphic decree for Aristotle and Callisthenes, and the scan-class witnesses of the Elenchi: the Byzantine paraphrast, Michael of Ephesus, Albert the Great, Giles of Rome) and carries as an appendix the cut of the four wills. Two working notes produced from these seats are deposited separately: Catalogues and Wills, and The Stone for a List.

entries.title: Catalogues and Wills: A Groundwork Note on the Peripatetic Transmission Texts — Relations Established, Readings Withheld (v0.3)
entries.creator: Sharks, Lee
entries.wiki: "Catalogues and Wills" is a groundwork note by Lee Sharks (v0.3, 6 September 2026) that establishes relations among the texts carrying the custody, enumeration and route of the Aristotelian and Theophrastan books, without reading them: the four Peripatetic wills preserved by Diogenes Laertius (Aristotle, Theophrastus, Strato, Lycon), the two catalogues attached to the lives of Aristotle and Theophrastus with their line-totals (445,270 and 232,808 στίχοι), Strabo XIII.1.54, Plutarch Sulla 26, Diogenes V.38 and Epistle VI. Its operations are counts, positions, co-occurrences and verbatim clauses. Among the relations it records: the will of Aristotle names no book, library, school or successor; Theophrastus's will gives all the books to one person, Neleus, and the garden, peripatos and houses to ten named friends in common as a sanctuary, under a prohibition on alienation, in adjacent clauses; Strato's will leaves Lycon all the books except those we ourselves have written; Lycon's separates books read from books unpublished and orders the latter published; the Theophrastan catalogue runs the alphabet twice before an unordered tail, contains nine internal doublets, shares twelve titles letter-for-letter with Aristotle's, and carries the entry Ὑπομνημάτων Ἀριστοτελικῶν ἢ Θεοφραστείων; Strabo narrates the custody with παρέδωκεν three times and asserts a first link the will lacks; Plutarch names Andronicus's act as drawing up the πίνακες now in circulation. The extant corpora are counted from the open Greek editions and set against the catalogued totals as two acts rather than as a loss ratio. The note lists eleven underdetermined areas as questions and records the corrections of a second reader. Companion to EA-CORPORA-12 (#1580), which seats the texts, and to The Stone for a List.
